project-title.text: Sound Sensing and Pan–Tilt Tracking for Meetings

platform.text:
AMD Zynq-7020 | PL + PS
Linux / PYNQ

intro-body.text: As people move and take turns speaking in meetings, fixed-direction devices need re-aiming. SoundSight targets meeting applications, with future use in robotics and embodied AI for sound direction and speaker identity.

system-scope.text: Zynq-7020 combines sound sensing and pointing. PL handles synchronous capture, frequency-domain correlation and pan–tilt PWM; PS handles 3D estimation, speaker verification and tracking. The final design adds local RGB touch control and direction-guided audio.

technical-heading.text: Key technical challenges and design choices

technical-body.text:
3D direction: Non-coplanar mics constrain azimuth and elevation; no distance estimate.
Scheduling: Direction updates continue during speaker scoring. Passing results grant a timed permit.
Motion: Direction quality, limits and mode gate motion. Axes default off, with stop and timeout guards.
Integration: Directional audio uses PCM and direction; touch links settings and status.

architecture-status.text:
Dashed paths await system integration; DAS has a PC reference.
Speaker verification uses one channel, not DAS output.

tetra-description.text: Four non-coplanar, tetrahedral mics provide six time-delay constraints. PL extracts correlation features; PS uses subsample interpolation, least squares and filtering to estimate azimuth and elevation, guiding pan–tilt aiming and directional audio.

async-description.text: A passing score grants a timed permit, so pan–tilt updates need not await each inference. This uses the current direction without guaranteed multi-speaker identity binding.

joint-heading.text:
Joint localization, verification
and pan–tilt operation

test-conditions.text:
48 kHz; direction window: 3 frames, at least 1 valid.
Level threshold: 12000 (PCM statistic).

joint-result.text: Both board trials combined localization reads, speaker scoring and pan–tilt commands with runtime fault values of 0. The user observed turning toward sound. This supports joint operation on one platform; commands do not confirm that the mechanism reached each target.

test-limitations.text: Both axes were enabled. The trials used one target template, threshold 0.45 and a 10 s permit. Each run completed 6 speaker evaluations before STOP as direction updates continued. Run 2 dropped 1 old localization result. Angular error, verification accuracy and long-term stability remain unverified.

outlook.text: Next: quantify direction/pointing error; test other speakers, real-mic beamforming and touch; pursue robotic hearing.
